reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: I read the resource-review contract, the resource assessment rubric, and the fresh-review framework, then reviewed the ClinicalImpression context, full structure report, deterministic aggregate, direct SearchParameters/HttpRestBehavior findings, and shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context. The deterministic aggregate was treated as prior context, not as the decision rule.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 ClinicalImpression was trial-use/FMM 0, so the base specification had weak compatibility pressure to preserve the resource unchanged. That lowers the standards-review burden for removing an experimental aggregate model, but it does not remove the clinical and audit migration risk for implementations that actually stored assessment summaries in this resource.

overall.oneLineConclusion: ClinicalImpression is absent from R6, so any real R4 use needs a resource-level migration program; endpoint and search breaks are important but derivative of that identity removal.

reasoning.thesisMd: The actual migration shape is whole-resource retirement, not an element-level remodel. R4 defines `ClinicalImpression` as a concrete DomainResource with required `status` and `subject` and local assessment, investigation, finding, prognosis, supporting-info, and note content. The supplied R6 package has no same-name StructureDefinition, package-index entry, direct resource reference, endpoint, or ClinicalImpression search-parameter surface. Therefore an R4 instance, generated class, REST route, and search client cannot be made R6-compatible by preserving or renaming a few fields.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: A migration program is already unavoidable for any implementation that used the resource. The likely work is policy-driven decomposition or archival: decide whether each ClinicalImpression should become one or more `Condition`, `Observation`, `DiagnosticReport`, `RiskAssessment`, `CarePlan`, encounter-linked notes, extensions, or legacy retained payloads, while preserving the original assessment identity and clinical grouping. This is not a simple rename because no single R6 resource preserves the full aggregate assessment shape.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Once the resource identity is removed, preventing additional local ClinicalImpression breaks has reduced leverage: old element names, old search parameters, and old endpoint advertisements only work if some legacy resource surface is retained. Retaining ClinicalImpression as a deprecated or retired R6 resource would be the main compatibility-preserving design, but that is a substantial base-model decision, not a low-cost alias. The remaining high-value compatibility work is migration guidance, maps, provenance/linkage advice, and explicit endpoint/search transition documentation.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The plausible less-breaking base alternative is to keep ClinicalImpression in R6 as deprecated/retired while steering new use to more specific resources. That would preserve most R4 wire/API compatibility, but it would also keep a low-FMM aggregate container in core, duplicate newer representations, and require ongoing validator, SDK, REST, and search support. Endpoint aliases or search redirects have the same dependency: without a retained resource or a clear one-to-one successor, they either fail to preserve semantics or effectively reintroduce the removed model. ConceptMaps, StructureMaps, and local profiles are important mitigations, but they are migration tools rather than low-cost base compatibility preservation.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The two direct behavior findings matter for ClinicalImpression clients: the R4 ClinicalImpression REST endpoint is no longer advertised in the R6 base CapabilityStatement inventory, and ClinicalImpression-only search parameters such as `status`, `subject`, `encounter`, `assessor`, `identifier`, `problem`, and finding/prognosis-related searches disappear with the removed endpoint. I treat these as important migration chores rather than independent drivers because they follow directly from the resource removal. The 11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were reviewed as context only and were not scored against ClinicalImpression per the resource-review rules.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate on the headline result: `majorMigrationAlreadyUnavoidable = Yes`, `resourceMigrationShape = removed-or-replaced-resource`, and `compatibilityLeverage = migration-program-dominates`. My added nuance is that this does not make mapping and transition guidance unimportant; it means the useful standards work is successor/migration guidance rather than trying to preserve individual ClinicalImpression paths after the resource surface is gone.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: The package evidence is strong that ClinicalImpression is absent from R6. The main uncertainty is policy/rationale: the local inputs did not include Patient Care work-group rationale, official ballot notes, or an authoritative R4-to-R6 ConceptMap/StructureMap. Actual deployment prevalence is also unknown, which matters because FMM 0 weakens the general stability claim but not the impact on adopters who did use the resource.

findingConsiderations.title: ClinicalImpression resource is absent from the R6 core package
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the decisive finding. An R4 `resourceType: "ClinicalImpression"` instance has no R6 base StructureDefinition, resource-type identity, generated model class, or native endpoint/search surface. That makes a resource-level migration unavoidable even though the R4 resource was only FMM 0/trial-use.

findingConsiderations.title: No single R6 resource preserves ClinicalImpression's aggregate assessment shape
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This finding explains why the migration is a policy/program issue rather than a mechanical rename. Adjacent R6 resources cover pieces of the clinical assessment, but without explicit linkage a decomposition can lose the original assessment grouping, status, previous-assessment relation, investigation sets, findings, prognosis, and narrative context.

findingConsiderations.title: Search parameters whose only R4 bases were removed resources disappear from the R6 search surface
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This directly affects ClinicalImpression queries, including common route shapes such as `ClinicalImpression?subject=...` or `ClinicalImpression?status=...`. It is important for client migration and test updates, but it is derivative of the removed resource; preserving the old searches would require a retained legacy endpoint or a documented successor query model.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The removed ClinicalImpression endpoint is a concrete runtime/API break for route discovery, generated clients, conformance tests, and generic servers. For this resource-level review, however, it does not independently change the conclusion because it follows from the same R6 resource identity removal.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 core removes the Resource $meta operation
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior changes can affect systems during a broad R6 migration, but this finding is not specific to ClinicalImpression and was not scored as a ClinicalImpression resource-level driver under the review instructions.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish or locate an authoritative ClinicalImpression migration note or map. It should say whether the intended R6 representation is archival retention, decomposition across resources, extensions/profiles, or another pattern, and how to preserve identifiers, status, subject, encounter, timing, assessor, previous assessment, investigations, findings, prognosis, supporting information, and notes.

For implementations with real ClinicalImpression data, treat the original assessment identity and grouping as clinically and audit-relevant. Preserve source linkage with identifiers, Provenance, extensions, or a local container strategy when decomposing into R6 resources.

Document the ClinicalImpression REST and search retirement explicitly. If backward-compatible servers support legacy ClinicalImpression routes or search aliases, label them as implementation compatibility behavior rather than R6 core support.

Do not spend standards effort preserving individual ClinicalImpression element names unless the resource identity itself is retained; field-level compatibility does not solve the dominant R6 validation/API break.

caveats: Official R6 ballot rationale and Patient Care work-group decisions were not present in the local inputs.
No authoritative cross-version ConceptMap or StructureMap for ClinicalImpression was found in the supplied packages.
R4 FMM 0 makes broad production prevalence uncertain; the migration conclusion is strongest for implementations that actually used ClinicalImpression.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were reviewed as context only and not scored as ClinicalImpression-specific findings.
